bull.b: Rapid, repeated sales growth indicates expanding product adoption and improving commercial reach. The company has set quarterly records while growing both direct-to-consumer and B2B channels, creating a stronger revenue base that can support operating leverage and broader distribution over the next several quarters.

Improving gross margin alongside slower expense growth shows that revenue is beginning to scale faster than the cost base. If this discipline persists, incremental sales could contribute more gross profit and narrow losses, strengthening the pathway toward sustained operating cash flow positivity.

NEXUS provides a meaningful growth engine, while shared components and existing equipment may allow higher output without proportionate capital spending. This combination can improve asset utilization, broaden the product portfolio, and increase revenue capacity if hiring and execution keep pace.

bear.b: The company remains far from breakeven despite strong sales growth, meaning its current revenue scale does not yet cover operating costs. Continued losses can erode equity, restrict strategic flexibility, and require faster margin improvement or higher volume before the business becomes self-funding.

Material cash consumption increases reliance on financing while the company expands inventory, production, and new products. Although Q3 cash use improved, management said that result benefited from working-capital timing, so durable cash-flow improvement remains unproven and financially important.

bear.t: Margin Pressure from Costs and Mix
bear.b: Higher material and landed costs are already reducing gross margin, while B2B growth generally carries lower margins than B2C. If the company absorbs tariff inflation to avoid price increases, stronger sales may translate into less incremental profit and delay progress toward profitability.
